acceptedWorkstreams.title: Define the handoff: when a mentor's note should become an instructor decision instead
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Mentors regularly give feedback on something that is really an assessment or a policy question, and the learner gets an answer from the wrong person. Work: list the signals (grading, deadline extension, plagiarism, a complaint about another learner) and for each, the exact sentence the mentor sends the learner and the person it goes to. Deliver the handoff list, the wording, and the response time the learner should expect after a handoff.

upvotes.reason: "Define the handoff: when a mentor's note should become an instructor decision instead" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.
Mentors answering grading or extension questions is a real escalation error. Exact learner wording plus an owner and response time makes the handoff usable, not just a list.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Measure the saving on five real projects instead of claiming one
acceptedWorkstreams.description: A guide that promises to save time has to show it once. Work: take five real projects, record mentor minutes per feedback round before and after using the loop, and report the range with the sample size and the parts that did not improve. Deliver the before-and-after table, the honest range, and the one step that turned out to cost more time than it saved, which is the part that makes the rest believable.

upvotes.reason: "Measure the saving on five real projects instead of claiming one" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it produces something checkable rather than an opinion, so the goal either moved or it did not.

A guide that claims time savings without a measured case repeats the unsourced-numbers problem the site is already being pulled up on. Five real projects, with the range and the step that cost more time, is the version a reviewer can check.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Write the fifteen-minute loop with a timer, so feedback has a bounded shape
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Mentors lose time not in the feedback itself but in deciding when it is finished. Work: define a loop with four timed steps (open the submission, read the diff or the project, write one thread reply with two specifics, set the next check), state what to do when the project needs longer than fifteen minutes, and what to send the learner in that case. Deliver the loop, the timer breakdown, and the three situations where stopping at fifteen minutes is the wrong call.
